name: Estuary and Salmon Restoration Program

funder.name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife

summary: Biennial grants for restoring and protecting near-shore habitat, estuaries and salmon habitat in Puget Sound, run as separate request-for-proposals tracks for restoration and protection, beach restoration small grants and regional pre-design.

amount.note: Limit for Restoration and Protection grants; other tracks have lower limits

eligibility.rule: Beach small grants: endorsed by a local MRC, Lead Entity, Lead Integrating Organization or Shore Friendly program
Not a stand-alone recreational access or chemical contamination remediation project
Work does not relieve obligatory payment or mitigation requirements

documents: Draft cost estimate or budget worksheet
Vicinity map, plus site plan or parcel map
All available design materials, for restoration projects
Portfolio Program Status Sheet, for portfolio projects

status.quote: Full Applications and Portfolio Applications Due May 22, 2026

deadline.quote: Full Applications and Portfolio Applications Due May 22, 2026

status.quote: Final Applications Due in PRISM March 31, 2026

deadline.quote: Final Applications Due in PRISM March 31, 2026

administered_by.quote: This grant program is managed by the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife with RCO administering the grants.

applicant_types.quote: Who May Apply? Federal agencies Local agencies Native American Tribes Nonprofit organizations Private institutions State agencies Universities and colleges

geography.quote: All projects must be in Puget Sound, east of Cape Flattery.

access.quote: Each grant program issues its own Request for Proposal with a specific grant application and review process.

window.quote: Estuary and Salmon Restoration Program funding is awarded every two years.

co_finance_required.quote: Match is not required for any ESRP grant program in the 2026 grant round.

eligibility.quote: Projects must be endorsed by at least one of the following local nearshore planning and conservation organizations: Marine Resources Committee, Lead Entity, Lead Integrating Organization, and/or Shore Friendly program.
Projects that primarily provide recreational access or remediate chemical contamination are not eligible as stand-alone projects
Grants will not be awarded for work that relieves obligatory payment or mitigation requirements.

after_award.quote: Sponsors are required to enter two progress reports a year for all funded projects using the PRISM Online progress reporting tool. Sponsors are also required to complete and submit a final report in PRISM Online at the completion of their projects.

documents.quote: Draft Cost Estimate or Budget Worksheet. You may create your own budget format for this proposal stage
Maps • General vicinity map for all projects • Site plan for restoration projects • Parcel map for acquisition projects
All Available Design Materials for Restoration Projects.
(Portfolio Program Applicants Only) Portfolio Program Status Sheet - please complete only the Pre-Proposal portion of the sheet

effort.quote: Pre-Proposals Due in PRISM February 9, 2026 Pre-Proposal Site Visits March 2, 2026 - March 26, 2026 Applicants Invited to Submit Full Proposals April 8, 2026
The BRSGP application process consists of three main requirements: 1) a pre-proposal, 2) a virtual site visit, and 3) a full application
